command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged inputs against their pinned sha256 (same bytes salmon used) =="
{ printf '%s  %s\n' 683eb19310c40bf1396e4718f45afa2ce86755717c0990f47a171f535d248ea1 cdna.fa.gz
  printf '%s  %s\n' 1198ed07e41fdf6f53710dfe4eee376d978e1bf61f0d9dcdd8b7ec2ce7c5432e ERR188026_sub_1.fq.gz
  printf '%s  %s\n' 6104ee4641702156ce3f5330b750db6fd461e597de43bb280158bc751a7e120a ERR188026_sub_2.fq.gz
} > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

echo "== kallisto index -- the memory-bound step (>8 GiB; this is why the recipe is r8g) =="
kallisto index -i idx cdna.fa.gz 2> index.log

echo "== kallisto quant =="
kallisto quant -i idx -o out -t 2 ERR188026_sub_1.fq.gz ERR188026_sub_2.fq.gz 2> quant.log

# Flatten artifacts to /tmp before declaring them as outputs (a /tmp/out parent would
# be root-owned by dockerd). Do NOT rm any staged input (cdna.fa.gz, the reads,
# salmon_quant.sf): host /tmp is sticky 1777 and stage-in runs as a different user,
# so the container gets EPERM and `rm -f` does not suppress EPERM -- it would kill
# the task under set -e. Keeping them is within the disk budget.
cp out/abundance.tsv abundance.tsv
cp out/run_info.json run_info.json

# ---- smoke check (runs inside the task so it can fail the task) ----
# No python/jq in this image; parse run_info.json with awk, correlate with awk+sort+join.
jget() { awk -F'[:,]' -v k="$1" '$0 ~ "\""k"\"" {gsub(/[^0-9]/,"",$2); print $2; exit}' run_info.json; }
NTARG=$(jget n_targets)
NPROC=$(jget n_processed)
NPS=$(jget n_pseudoaligned)
ROWS=$(tail -n +2 abundance.tsv | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
TPMSUM=$(awk 'NR>1{s+=$5}END{printf "%.0f", s}' abundance.tsv)

# Cross-code vs salmon: SPEARMAN (rank) of TPM on transcripts BOTH tools detect.
# Rank, not raw-value Pearson, is the honest claim -- salmon and kallisto use different
# effective-length / multimapping models, so absolute TPMs differ (raw log-TPM Pearson
# ~0.61) while abundance RANK-ORDER agrees strongly. Two independent EM quantifiers on
# identical reads+reference; the floor is set by that method agreement, not by the
# observed value. A broken quant decorrelates far below.
awk 'FNR==NR{ if(FNR>1) st[$1]=$4; next }
     FNR>1 && $5>0 && ($1 in st) && st[$1]>0 { print $1, $5, st[$1] }' salmon_quant.sf abundance.tsv > shared.txt
NBOTH=$(wc -l < shared.txt | tr -d ' ')
sort -k2,2g shared.txt | awk '{print $1, NR}' | sort > rk.txt
sort -k3,3g shared.txt | awk '{print $1, NR}' | sort > rs.txt
SPEAR=$(join rk.txt rs.txt | awk '{k=$2;s=$3;n++;sk+=k;ss+=s;skk+=k*k;sss+=s*s;sks+=k*s}
  END{printf "%.4f", (n*sks-sk*ss)/sqrt((n*skk-sk*sk)*(n*sss-ss*ss))}')
PCT=$(awk -v a="$NPS" -v b="$NPROC" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", 100*a/b}')

{
  echo "n_targets            $NTARG   want exactly 465769   (sequences in the Ensembl-116 cDNA FASTA)"
  echo "fragments_processed  $NPROC   want exactly 200000"
  echo "quant_rows           $ROWS   want exactly 465769   (== n_targets, every transcript)"
  echo "tpm_sum              $TPMSUM   want exactly 1000000  (per-million normalisation)"
  echo "pct_pseudoaligned    $PCT   want 88..96           (observed 92.1)"
  echo "spearman_vs_salmon   $SPEAR   want >= 0.85          (both-expressed n=$NBOTH; observed 0.9120)"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt

test "$NTARG"  -eq 465769
test "$NPROC"  -eq 200000
test "$ROWS"   -eq 465769
test "$TPMSUM" -eq 1000000
awk -v p="$PCT"   'BEGIN{ if (p>=88 && p<=96) exit 0; print "pct_pseudoaligned " p " outside band"; exit 1 }'
awk -v s="$SPEAR" 'BEGIN{ if (s>=0.85)        exit 0; print "spearman " s " below 0.85"; exit 1 }'
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
